clauses.reason: Section 1 (each Federal department and agency, in consultation with the Federal Civil Defense Administration, prepares plans for providing its personnel, materials, facilities and services under section 302 of the Federal Civil Defense Act during a civil-defense emergency). Terminated by express revocation: section 3015 of Executive Order 11490 of October 28, 1969 (34 FR 17567, govinfo printing) states that the listed orders are hereby revoked and its item 4 names Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952 (the OCR of the held page prints the date as April IT, 1952 and the section title as Revoiced Orders). The signature block is dated October 28, 1969 and the order has no effective-date wording, so the end is dated on signing, 1969-10-28 (a reading, disclosed). The clause was amended, not ended, by Executive Order 10438 (1953-03-13), Executive Order 10773 (1958-07-01) and Executive Order 11051 section 603(b) (1962-09-27); each is recorded as a later event on the clauses it reaches (strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21: the clause continues, amended, until the parent ends). Executive Order 11051 also revokes 10438 and 10773 by a general supersession list without touching 10346 itself, and does not end this order. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10346 (17 FR 3477; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10346, Preparation by Federal Agencies of Civil Defense Emergency Plans, signed April 17, 1952, under the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950. Inventory: three sections (agency civil-defense plans; continuity-of-functions plans; assistance by the Federal Civil Defense Administrator). The dossier listed eight clauses, most of them the paragraphs and prorate schedule of a Department of Agriculture lemon regulation printed on the same page; the inventory is corrected to the three sections by absolute character spans of the held text. Ending: section 3015 of Executive Order 11490 of October 28, 1969 revokes Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952 by number (its item 4). The machine ACT record for pair 10346 and 11490 that points to section 501 is not the revoking provision; the alternative record that quotes sections 3011 to 3015 and ends with the line naming 10346 is selected. The U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note and the OFR catalog also report revocation by Executive Order 11490 on 1969-10-28. Amendments (later events, not ends): Executive Order 10438 (1953-03-13) transfers functions of the National Security Resources Board and its Chairman under 10346 to the Director of Defense Mobilization; Executive Order 10773 (1958-07-01) substitutes references to the Federal Civil Defense Administrator and Administration and to the Office of Defense Mobilization; Executive Order 11051 section 603(b) (1962-09-27) substitutes references to the Office of Emergency Planning or the Department of Defense. The U.S. Code note also lists Executive Order 10782 among amending orders; its held text does not cite 10346, so no event is recorded for it. Executive Order 10529 of 1954 cites section 3 of 10346 and does not amend or end it. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

savings.reason: Section 3014 of Executive Order 11490 keeps existing assignments of functions made by statute, order or directive except as provided in section 3015, and section 3015 revokes 10346; the planning duties of 10346 were reassigned afresh by Executive Order 11490 (new sections for each department) and are not residual effects of 10346. No held source shows a continuing independent effect of the revoked order, and the agencies' completed plans carry no authority of 10346 (Executive Order 11490 section 3011 says plans confer no authority to put them into effect).
